subject: Clarify compute-units vs token billing for Chat / Responses / legacy endpoints
messages:
From: Nathan Young <nathan@brightanchor.com>

Cc: BrightAnchor Procurement <procurement@brightanchor.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Quick ask on billing units (Chat vs Responses vs legacy)

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightAnchor's search team liked the latency profile. Procurement asked for a concise breakdown of how we would be billed if we migrate a mix of old chat calls and new Responses API calls. Specifically:

- Do "Responses" calls map 1:1 to token units or do they use a separate compute-unit SKU?
- How do legacy Chat Completions map to the new billing for comparison on our forecast sheet?
- Any guidance on how prefix caching and embeddings calls influence monthly unit consumption?

We have a model of ~2M messages/month today (short chats, average 60 tokens generated) and a plan to add ~500k shorter Responses-style requests (structured outputs) if latency/cost looks good.

Also, are there standard first-year discounts for committed reserved capacity? Procurement expects a starter discount ask.

Can you send a short doc we can share with finance?

Best,
Nathan
Senior PM, BrightAnchor

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Nathan Young <nathan@brightanchor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask on billing units (Chat vs Responses vs legacy)

Hi Nathan — looping in Laura (pricing) and Rishi (billing) to make sure we cover everything.

High-level answers up front:
1) Responses vs Chat: base billing is token-based across hosted APIs, but the measurable unit differs by endpoint. "Responses" groups input+output tokens and applies the Responses unit price; Chat Completions historically billed per-context token and had different per-token multipliers for system vs user vs assistant. For forecasting, assume Responses unit = sum(input tokens + output tokens) * Responses rate, and Chat = sum(tokens) * Chat rate.

2) Compute-units / hidden SKUs: we surface per-token pricing on the rate card; under the hood we may allocate compute units for burst and model size which affects eligible discounts. For committed Dedicated (reserved capacity) we map consumption to a committed GPU-hours baseline (we can translate your token forecasts into that baseline).

3) Caching & embeddings: prefix/KV caching reduces billable tokens only if full response assembly is skipped — generally it reduces compute and tokens for repeated prompts. Embeddings are billed separately (per-embedding unit) and do not consume chat/response token units.

I'll attach a short rate card extract and a worked example using your numbers. Laura/Rishi — can you confirm the example and usable first-year discount tiers (10/15/20% at 6/12/24mo commits)?

Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick ask on billing units (Chat vs Responses vs legacy)

Nathan — attaching a short worked example and the current hosted rate card (PDF). See the two tabs in the attached spreadsheet:

- "Token-Map": converts your 2M chat messages + 500k Responses into monthly billable token totals under both the Chat and Responses pricing lines.
- "Commit-Offer": shows three commitment tiers with example discounts and the equivalent committed GPU-hours (for Dedicated mapping).

Key callouts:
- For short generated responses (~60 tokens), Responses pricing is about 8-12% cheaper than calling the legacy Chat endpoint for equivalent payloads because Responses bundles some of the system token overhead; exact delta depends on system/preamble size.
- If you use heavy prefix/KV caching for repeat queries, effective tokens consumed drop up to ~30% for qualifying calls — we'll annotate which routes are cache-eligible.
- Embeddings are billed entirely separately and should not be folded into the token forecast for Chat/Responses.

Attachments: Redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf (extract), usage_estimate_brightanchor.xlsx

If you want, Connor and I can run a one-hour pricing workshop with your finance/procurement next week to walk the spreadsheet and lock a deal cadence.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
